name: ses-lockdown
description: Tether Secure Browser v1.7.4 (pre-exam readiness + safe lockdown activation: fixes three confirmed problems — (1) pre-exam remediation was too restrictive (a screen-saver-level always-on-top overlay could obstruct Task Manager during TeamViewer/display remediation); (2) BLOCKED display decisions were mislabelled as genuine additional-display detections (active&&!ready and inconclusive topology queries both showed 'Additional display connected' with no real evidence — see displayEnforcementLogic.ts's DisplayBlockingReason taxonomy); (3) the exam timer/question content could begin before secure-client attestation and native lockdown activation actually completed. New two-phase lifecycle: PHASE 1 PRE-EXAM READINESS runs every mandatory native precheck (prohibited applications, remote session, display topology) with NO strict overlay and NO submission/timer created, showing a calm in-page remediation screen (Task Manager/Alt+Tab/Windows display settings all remain usable) until an explicit 'Begin examination' action; PHASE 2 SECURE ACTIVATION then creates the submission (PREPARING, no timer/content yet), issues/consumes the launch manifest, requires VERIFIED attestation, re-runs a FRESH native check (closing the race where TeamViewer/a display appears between precheck and Begin examination — see main.ts's lockdown:activate-secure-exam-lockdown), activates native lockdown atomically, and only then calls the new authoritative POST /api/submissions/[id]/activate (see Submission.activatedAt in the main repo's prisma/schema.prisma) before the timer starts and Question 1 becomes reachable — enforced server-side (src/lib/secureClientActivation.ts), never merely by hiding React content. Previously v1.7.3 (sandboxed-preload hotfix: dist/preload.js is now bundled with esbuild (--bundle --external:electron) instead of plain tsc output, so it no longer contains a relative require("./shared") that the sandboxed Electron preload require() polyfill rejects with 'module not found' — that failure previously aborted the entire preload script BEFORE contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld ran, silently disabling window.sesLockdown (and therefore getDisplayCount, breaking SINGLE_DISPLAY_REQUIRED exams) with no visible error. sandbox:true/contextIsolation:true/nodeIntegration:false are unchanged; the bridge surface exposed to the page is unchanged. See verifyPreloadBundle.ts (build-time regression guard) and sandboxPreloadRuntimeCheck.ts (runtime regression check against the real built preload). Previously v1.7.2 (mid-exam remote-session monitoring: the REMOTE_DESKTOP_SESSION capability is now polled continuously while an exam is ACTIVE, not just at preflight — see remoteSessionMonitor.ts/remoteSessionMonitorLogic.ts — reusing the existing REMOTE_CONTROL_SOFTWARE_DETECTED/PROHIBITED_APPLICATION_CLOSED event model, deduplicated state transitions, and an event-triggered evidence frame; also fixes a latent poll-serialization bug in processDetection.ts where a `.finally()`-wrapped promise's identity could never match its own in-flight guard, silently freezing during-exam process detection at its first scan result for the rest of the exam. Built on v1.7.1's destroyed-window crash fix: restoreLockdownControls/reportAuditFactBestEffort could throw 'Object has been destroyed' when the BrowserWindow's closed event fired, crashing the main process — restoration is now independent of any window and audit reporting is routed through a shared isWindowUsable/runOnWindowBestEffort guard. Built on v1.7.0's Tether Windows Lockdown Hardening v1 — adds a Windows-only process-detection service for known remote-control/debugging/virtualization/screen-capture applications, a remote-session/VM indicator, a main-owned preflight gate and during-exam blocking overlay, an idempotent restoration lifecycle, and materially strengthened Electron hardening: a permission allowlist, denied navigation/window.open/downloads, packaged-build DevTools prevention, rejected unsafe command-line switches, and blocked browser-chrome keyboard shortcuts. See docs/tether-windows-lockdown-hardening-v1.md. v1.4.0 and v1.5.0 were development-only, never distributed.)

scripts.build: tsc -p tsconfig.json && npm run bundle:preload && npm run verify:preload-bundle
scripts.pack: npm run build && electron-builder --dir && npm run verify:package
scripts.dist:win: npm run build && electron-builder --win --dir && npm run embed:icon && electron-builder --win --prepackaged release/win-unpacked && npm run verify:package -- release/win-unpacked
